design.affected_system: waste collection, recycling, street cleaning, illegal-dumping, and sanitation response
alternatives: rank verified high-consequence candidates for sanitation asset and service improvement portfolio
select a risk-, equity-, and lifecycle-balanced portfolio for sanitation asset and service improvement portfolio
pair failure, demand, equity, cost, and lifecycle portfolio optimization with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Requests, route events, tonnage, inspections, dumping evidence, contamination, and completion remain distinct.
Waste generation and service demand are measured or modeled with declared coverage.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: fund only already-committed work for sanitation asset and service improvement portfolio.

constraints.description: The sanitation, waste, and street cleanliness prioritize must respect declared capital, operating, maintenance, and delivery budgets.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: sanitation commissioner and waste operations chief
design.decision_question: Which vehicles, containers, depots, public bins, route tools, and prevention measures should be funded?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The sanitation, waste, and street cleanliness prioritize must respect declared capital, operating, maintenance, and delivery budgets.
independence_key.decision_object: sanitation asset and service improvement portfolio
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for sanitation asset and service improvement portfolio passes documented checks for cost, benefit, service life, dependencies, deliverability, and maintenance burden.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: failure, demand, equity, cost, and lifecycle portfolio optimization
independence_key.primary_outcome: expected sanitation service failure and overflow burden

design.intended_claim: A versioned prioritize design for comparing declared alternatives affecting sanitation asset and service improvement portfolio, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: expected sanitation service failure and overflow burden
distributional gap in expected sanitation service failure and overflow burden
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not report modeled cleanliness or service gains as observed outcomes.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.
design.reference_implementation_note: Tier-D template deep.public-service.sanitation-workload.v1 (Sanitation-related request workload planning) supplies a bounded reference workflow for this design axis. The mapping does not establish complete city-specific inputs, external validity, deployment, adoption, or impact.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for sanitation asset and service improvement portfolio passes documented checks for cost, benefit, service life, dependencies, deliverability, and maintenance burden.

design.title: Prioritize sanitation assets and service improvements
transportability_risks: Collection systems, housing form, waste law, contracts, markets, and reporting behavior differ.
Request labels and tonnage do not fully capture cleanliness or illegal dumping.

family.affected_system: waste collection, recycling, street cleaning, illegal-dumping, and sanitation response
claim_boundary: Service requests measure reported workload, not verified incidents, need, harm, or resolution.
Assignments and schedules are proposed operations, not completed work or public outcomes.
Design records do not establish agency adoption, deployment, productivity, or resident impact.
family.decision_owner: sanitation commissioner and waste operations chief
family.description: Eight decisions for sanitation signal diagnosis, workload forecasting, asset investment, facility siting, crew allocation, route scheduling, disruption stress, and intervention evaluation.
family.title: Sanitation, waste, and street cleanliness

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
